topicName: Crop Husbandry of Cereals and Legumes
description: This topic covers the production practices of major cereal crops such as maize and rice and legume crops such as beans and groundnuts grown in Tanzania, including their ecological requirements, planting, fertiliser use, pest and disease control, harvesting and storage, plus the role of legumes in improving soil fertility through nitrogen fixation.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the most important cereal staple food crop in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Maize is the leading cereal and staple food for most Tanzanians, used to make ugali and other foods.

mcq.questionText: Legumes improve soil fertility mainly because they can fix:
mcq.explanation: Legumes house Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules, which convert atmospheric nitrogen into a form plants can use, enriching the soil.

mcq.questionText: The bacteria responsible for nitrogen fixation in legume root nodules are called:
mcq.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live symbiotically in legume root nodules and fix atmospheric nitrogen for the plant.

mcq.questionText: Which crop is mostly grown under irrigation schemes in areas such as the Kilombero and Mbarali valleys of Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Rice (paddy) requires plenty of water and is widely grown in lowland irrigation schemes such as Kilombero and Mbarali.

mcq.questionText: Which cereal crop is best suited to dry areas with low and unreliable rainfall because of its drought tolerance?
mcq.explanation: Sorghum and millet are drought tolerant and are grown in semi-arid regions such as Dodoma, Singida and Shinyanga.

mcq.questionText: Crop rotation that includes legumes is recommended because legumes:

options.text: Use up all the soil nitrogen
Add nitrogen to the soil for the next crop

mcq.explanation: Because legumes fix nitrogen, including them in a rotation enriches the soil so that the following cereal crop benefits from the added nitrogen.

mcq.questionText: The recommended spacing for maize in pure stand under good rainfall is approximately:

options.text: 90 cm between rows and 30 cm within rows
10 cm between rows and 5 cm within rows
3 m between rows and 3 m within rows
200 cm between rows and 100 cm within rows

mcq.explanation: A common recommended maize spacing is about 90 cm between rows and 30 cm within the row, giving a good plant population.

mcq.questionText: Which fertiliser is commonly applied to cereals such as maize as a top dressing to promote vegetative (leaf and stem) growth?
mcq.explanation: Nitrogenous fertilisers such as urea or CAN are used as top dressing on maize to boost leaf and stem (vegetative) growth.

mcq.questionText: Maize stalk borer is best described as a:

options.text: Pest that bores into the maize stem
Type of weed in maize fields

mcq.explanation: The stalk borer is an insect pest whose larvae tunnel into the maize stem, weakening the plant and reducing yield.

mcq.questionText: Why is timely weeding important in cereal and legume fields?

options.text: Weeds add nitrogen to the crop
Weeds compete with crops for water, light and nutrients

mcq.explanation: Weeds compete with crops for water, nutrients, light and space, and may harbour pests, so early weeding raises yields.

mcq.questionText: Groundnuts are unusual among legumes because their pods develop:

options.text: Underground after the flowers push pegs into the soil
High up on the main stem

mcq.explanation: After fertilisation, groundnut flowers form pegs that grow down into the soil where the pods then develop underground.

mcq.questionText: To reduce losses during storage of maize grain, the grain should first be:

options.text: Properly dried to a low moisture content
Left on the cob in the field for a year

mcq.explanation: Drying grain to a low moisture content prevents mould growth and reduces attack by storage pests such as weevils.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a legume crop grown for its protein-rich seeds in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Common beans are a widely grown legume in Tanzania, valued as an affordable source of protein.

mcq.questionText: A common storage pest that attacks dry maize and bean grains in stores is the:
mcq.explanation: Weevils bore into stored grains and cause serious losses; they are controlled by drying, clean stores and approved storage chemicals.

mcq.questionText: Which practice helps to break pest and disease cycles in cereal production?

options.text: Growing the same crop on the same land every season
Planting only at the end of the rains

mcq.explanation: Rotating crops denies specific pests and diseases their host plant each season, helping to break their life cycles.

fib.questionText: The bacteria found in legume root nodules that fix nitrogen are called _____.
fib.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live in legume root nodules and convert atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form.

fib.questionText: The cereal crop that is the main staple food in Tanzania, used to make ugali, is _____.
fib.explanation: Maize is the leading staple cereal and is processed into flour for ugali.

fib.questionText: Rice grows best in waterlogged or flooded fields known as paddy fields and is mainly grown under _____ in Tanzania.
fib.explanation: Because rice needs plenty of water, it is largely grown in irrigation schemes such as Kilombero and Mbarali.

fib.questionText: Drought-tolerant cereals such as sorghum and _____ are grown in dry regions like Dodoma and Singida.
fib.explanation: Sorghum and millet tolerate low rainfall and are common in the semi-arid central regions.

fib.questionText: Legumes are an important source of the nutrient _____ in human and animal diets.
fib.explanation: Legume seeds such as beans and groundnuts are rich in protein, making them valuable in the diet.

fib.questionText: Applying nitrogenous fertiliser such as urea to maize after germination to boost leaf growth is called _____ .
fib.explanation: Top dressing is the application of fertiliser to a growing crop, usually nitrogen for vegetative growth.

fib.questionText: Before storage, maize and bean grains must be properly _____ to lower their moisture content and prevent mould.
fib.explanation: Drying reduces moisture, preventing mould and reducing attack by storage pests.

fib.questionText: Groundnut pods develop _____ the soil after pegs from the flowers grow downwards.
fib.explanation: After fertilisation the pegs push into the ground and the pods develop below the soil surface.

fib.questionText: Growing different crops on the same land in a planned sequence over seasons is called _____ .
fib.explanation: Crop rotation maintains fertility and breaks pest and disease cycles.

fib.questionText: The insect pest whose larvae tunnel into the maize stem is the maize stalk _____ .
fib.explanation: The stalk borer bores into the stem, weakening the plant and reducing yield.

tf.questionText: Legumes can add nitrogen to the soil through their root nodules.
tf.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria in the root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen, enriching the soil.

tf.questionText: Rice can be grown successfully in very dry areas without any irrigation or flooding.
tf.explanation: Rice needs plenty of water and is grown in flooded paddy fields or under irrigation, not in dry areas.

tf.questionText: Sorghum and millet are more drought tolerant than maize.
tf.explanation: Sorghum and millet survive low rainfall better than maize, so they are grown in semi-arid regions.

tf.questionText: Weeds help crops grow by supplying them with extra nutrients.
tf.explanation: Weeds compete with crops for nutrients, water and light and can lower yields.

tf.questionText: Storing grain while it is still wet helps to keep it safe from weevils.
tf.explanation: Wet grain encourages mould and pests; grain must be dried before storage.

tf.questionText: Including legumes in a crop rotation can reduce the amount of nitrogen fertiliser needed by the next crop.
tf.explanation: Legumes leave nitrogen in the soil, so the following cereal needs less nitrogen fertiliser.

tf.questionText: Maize is the leading staple food crop for most people in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Maize is the main staple, eaten widely as ugali across the country.

tf.questionText: Groundnut pods grow high up on the stem above the ground.
tf.explanation: Groundnut pods develop underground after pegs push into the soil.

tf.questionText: Top dressing with a nitrogenous fertiliser such as urea promotes vegetative growth in maize.
tf.explanation: Nitrogen encourages leaf and stem growth, so urea or CAN is used as top dressing on maize.

tf.questionText: Crop rotation has no effect on pests and diseases in the field.
tf.explanation: Crop rotation breaks pest and disease cycles by removing their host crop each season.

summary.questionText: State two reasons why legumes are important in improving soil fertility.
summary.correctAnswer: They fix atmospheric nitrogen through Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules, and their leaf fall and roots add organic matter to the soil.
summary.explanation: Legumes enrich the soil with nitrogen and organic matter, benefiting following crops.

summary.questionText: Name three cereal crops grown in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Maize, rice and sorghum (also wheat and millet).
summary.explanation: These are the main cereals grown across different regions of Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Give three legume crops grown in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Beans, groundnuts and cowpeas (also pigeon peas and soya beans).
summary.explanation: These legumes provide protein and improve soil fertility.

summary.questionText: Outline the main steps in land preparation for maize.
summary.correctAnswer: Clearing the land, ploughing, harrowing to break clods and make a fine seedbed, and levelling before planting.
summary.explanation: Good land preparation gives a fine, weed-free seedbed for even germination.

summary.questionText: Why is rice mostly grown under irrigation in Tanzania?
summary.correctAnswer: Because rice requires large amounts of water and grows best in flooded paddy fields, which irrigation schemes can provide reliably.
summary.explanation: Irrigation supplies the constant water rice needs, as in Kilombero and Mbarali.

summary.questionText: Describe two methods of controlling storage pests such as weevils in grains.
summary.correctAnswer: Drying grain well and storing it in clean, dry stores, and treating stored grain with approved storage insecticides or using airtight containers.
summary.explanation: Drying and clean, treated storage reduce losses from weevils and other pests.

summary.questionText: State two reasons why weeding is necessary in a cereal field.
summary.correctAnswer: To reduce competition for water, nutrients, light and space, and to remove plants that may harbour pests and diseases.
summary.explanation: Weeding raises yields by reducing competition and pest harbourage.

summary.questionText: Explain the importance of crop rotation in cereal and legume production.
summary.correctAnswer: It maintains soil fertility (especially when legumes are included), breaks pest and disease cycles, and controls weeds, leading to better yields.
summary.explanation: Rotation keeps soil productive and reduces pest, disease and weed build-up.

summary.questionText: Give two economic importances of cereals and legumes to Tanzanian farmers.
summary.correctAnswer: They provide food for the family and surplus for sale to earn income, and crops such as rice and groundnuts can be sold in markets or exported to earn money.
summary.explanation: Cereals and legumes provide both food security and income.

summary.questionText: Why should grain be dried before storage?
summary.correctAnswer: Drying lowers moisture content, which prevents mould growth and reduces attack by storage pests such as weevils, keeping the grain in good condition.
summary.explanation: Low moisture protects stored grain from spoilage and pests.

hoq.questionText: A farmer in Iringa harvested very low maize yields after growing maize on the same field for five consecutive years. The best long-term advice to improve fertility and yield is to:

options.text: Continue growing maize but plant it more densely
Introduce a crop rotation that includes a legume such as beans
Harvest the maize while still very wet

hoq.explanation: Continuous maize depletes soil nitrogen and builds up pests. Rotating with a legume restores nitrogen through fixation and breaks pest cycles, improving yields.

hoq.questionText: A farmer applies a heavy dose of nitrogenous fertiliser to a bean crop expecting higher seed yield, but instead gets many leaves and few pods. The most likely explanation is that:

options.text: Beans already fix their own nitrogen, so excess nitrogen encourages leaf growth at the expense of pods
Beans cannot absorb any nitrogen from fertiliser
Nitrogen fertiliser always kills bean flowers
Beans need no nutrients at all to produce pods

hoq.explanation: Legumes fix their own nitrogen, so extra nitrogen fertiliser promotes vegetative (leafy) growth rather than flowering and pod formation, reducing seed yield.

hoq.questionText: Two neighbouring farmers store maize after harvest. Farmer A dries the grain well and keeps it in a clean, treated store; Farmer B stores moist grain in a dirty store. After three months Farmer B's maize is mouldy and full of weevils. This best demonstrates that:

options.text: Moisture and poor hygiene encourage mould and storage pests
Maize cannot be stored for more than one month
Drying grain makes it more attractive to pests

hoq.explanation: High moisture and unclean stores favour mould and weevil multiplication. Proper drying and clean, treated stores prevent these losses, as shown by Farmer A.
